faq.a: Abdulfattah represents Arabic عَبْدُ الْفَتَّاح, meaning servant of the Opener/Judge.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulfattah?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الْفَتَّاح (ʿAbd al-Fattāḥ).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdulfattah?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; al-Fattāḥ is related to ف ت ح (f-t-ḥ).
Abdulfattah is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Fattāḥ, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdulfattah as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abdulfattah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of the Opener/Judge; the compound combines عبد with al-Fattāḥ.
The supplied “ab-dul-fat-tah” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.q: Is Abdulfattah a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
